Books and Papers, in Reading Order
For Child-Rearing
Jean Liedloff, The Continuum Concept (1975) — a foundational natural-child-rearing book based on Liedloff’s time with the Ye’kuana. Read it as provocative observation rather than settled anthropology.
Michaeleen Doucleff, Hunt, Gather, Parent (2021) — a practical, accessible book about children participating in family life, autonomy, and distributed care.
Practical Community-Building Guides
Diana Leafe Christian, Creating a Life Together — start here for sequencing, membership, money, land, and agreements.
Yana Ludwig, Building Belonging — a whole-systems guide to intentional community.
Governance Manuals
Rau and Koch-Gonzalez, Many Voices One Song — a practical sociocracy manual.
Schaub and colleagues, Building United Judgment — consensus decision-making.
Ludwig and Gimnig, The Cooperative Culture Handbook — exercises for cooperation, conflict, and group culture.
What Helps Communities Last—and Whether Longevity Is Enough
Dmitry Orlov, Communities That Abide — an uncomfortable argument that long-surviving communities often rely on communal property, separation, boundaries, and binding ideology. Cohesion and capture can resemble each other from a distance.
Rubin, Willis, and Ludwig, “Measuring Success in Intentional Communities” — asks whether longevity alone is a meaningful measure when a community may persist without members flourishing.
Rosabeth Moss Kanter, Commitment and Community — a classic comparison of nineteenth-century communes and the practices that built commitment.
Benjamin Zablocki, Alienation and Charisma — field research on communes and the role of charisma.
Jo Freeman, “The Tyranny of Structurelessness” (1970) — the classic argument that hidden hierarchy can be harder to challenge than explicit authority.
For the Zapatistas
Gloria Muñoz Ramírez and Subcomandante Marcos, The Fire and the Word — movement formation, practice-before-theory, autonomous institutions, and the original Good Government Boards.
The Zapatistas’ own Enlace Zapatista archive, especially their 2023 explanations of the new autonomy.
